_comment: Example credo LAN peer relay config. The easy way to create this is NOT to copy this file but to run '/credo:peer-lan init <peer-ip> ...' (or 'credo-peer-lan.py init <peer-ip> ...'), which writes ~/.claude/credo/peer-lan.json for you, token-less, and prints this machine's own address. The relay is a no-op until the config exists; once it does, it starts automatically on session start (one daemon per machine) and can be disabled with CREDO_PEER_LAN set to 0/false/no/off.
_peers_comment: Routing is ADDRESS-based: a peer is identified by its host:port, NOT by a name. List each OTHER machine's LAN address. A plain "IP" uses listen_port; "IP:PORT" overrides the port. Multiple entries = multiple machines. You always enter the TARGET machine's LAN IP: for a WSL2 machine that is its WINDOWS HOST IP (not the 172.x WSL IP); for native Linux its own LAN IP. Run 'credo-peer-lan.py whoami' on each machine to print its own address so you never have to guess which IP to enter.
_token_comment: The shared token is OPTIONAL and omitted here, so the relay runs TOKEN-LESS - the casual default for a trusted home LAN. WITHOUT a token, any device that can reach listen_host:listen_port can send messages to your sessions (gated only by the receiving session's own consent prompt; the relay never forges a trusted sender). To restrict messaging to your own devices, add the SAME non-empty "token" on every machine - recommended on untrusted or company networks. A machine whose token differs from a token-requiring peer is rejected by that peer.
